# View rollout proposal

This is a SQL-only authored local release-review fixture. Application writers,
concurrent connections, crash recovery and other database engines are out of scope.
Consumers execute the literal queries in readers.py. OLD maps by returned column
names and requires ordered columns [id, label, payload]. NEW requires
[id, title, payload]. Both require exact full ordered rows and binary payloads.
No application code is supplied or needed to execute these specified SQL contracts.

Order: (1) apply 001_schema.sql, OLD active; (2) apply 002_up.sql with OLD still
active; (3) apply 003_new_writes.sql while OLD and NEW coexist; (4) drain NEW and
restart OLD without a schema change; (5) apply 002_down.sql with OLD active.
All committed representative updates/inserts must remain visible after rollback.
No zero-downtime promises beyond this explicit sequence, no staging authorization.

Review this proposal as supplied; do not modify SQL or reader contracts. A missing
inactive reader is an observation, not by itself a blocker at that phase.
OLD = 'SELECT * FROM public_items ORDER BY id'
NEW = 'SELECT id, title, payload FROM public_items ORDER BY id'
CREATE TABLE items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, payload BLOB NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO items VALUES(1, '첫 항목', x'00ff'), (2, 'keep', x'');
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title, payload FROM items;
UPDATE items SET title='updated', payload=x'fe00' WHERE id=1;
INSERT INTO items VALUES(3, 'new', x'80');
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -B - <<'PY'
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import sqlite3

files = sorted(p for p in Path('.').iterdir() if p.is_file())
before = {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in files}
readers = runpy.run_path('readers.py')
queries = {name: readers[name] for name in ('OLD', 'NEW')}
labels = {'OLD': ('id', 'label', 'payload'), 'NEW': ('id', 'title', 'payload')}
initial = [(1, '첫 항목', b'\\x00\\xff'), (2, 'keep', b'')]
written = [(1, 'updated', b'\\xfe\\x00'), (2, 'keep', b''), (3, 'new', b'\\x80')]
phases = [
    (1, '001_schema.sql', {'OLD'}, initial),
    (2, '002_up.sql', {'OLD'}, initial),
    (3, '003_new_writes.sql', {'OLD', 'NEW'}, written),
    (4, None, {'OLD'}, written),
    (5, '002_down.sql', {'OLD'}, written),
]
con = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
print('Python sqlite3 / SQLite', sqlite3.sqlite_version)
print('Literal readers:', queries)
print('Expected labels:', labels)
for checkpoint, script, active, expected_rows in phases:
    if script:
        con.executescript(Path(script).read_text())
        con.commit()
    assert not con.in_transaction
    print('\\nCHECKPOINT', checkpoint, script or '(no SQL: drain NEW, restart OLD)', 'active=', sorted(active))
    print('Expected complete ordered rows:', repr(expected_rows))
    backing = con.execute('SELECT id, title, payload FROM items ORDER BY id').fetchall()
    assert backing == expected_rows
    assert all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in backing)
    print('Committed backing rows:', repr(backing))
    for name, query in queries.items():
        status = 'active' if name in active else 'inactive'
        try:
            cursor = con.execute(query)
            observed_labels = tuple(col[0] for col in cursor.description)
            rows = cursor.fetchall()
            exact_rows = rows == expected_rows and all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in rows)
            compatible = observed_labels == labels[name] and exact_rows
            print(name, status, 'labels=', observed_labels, 'rows=', repr(rows),
                  'payload_hex=', [row[2].hex() for row in rows], 'compatible=', compatible)
            assert exact_rows
            assert observed_labels == labels['OLD' if checkpoint in (1, 5) else 'NEW']
            assert compatible == (name == ('OLD' if checkpoint in (1, 5) else 'NEW'))
        except sqlite3.OperationalError as error:
            print(name, status, 'ERROR:', str(error))
            assert name == 'NEW' and checkpoint in (1, 5)
            assert str(error) == 'no such column: title'
    print('View:', con.execute(\"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='view' AND name='public_items'\").fetchone()[0])
con.close()
after = {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in files}
assert before == after
print('\\nPASS: all five checkpoint observations match assertions; supplied file hashes unchanged.')
PY"
